applies_why: The judge does not ground UNDERDETERMINED on the fact that a single verse fails to state a link or its contrary; it grounds it on the curse limb having been dropped, leaving no live link.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse.
room: Phrase: 'That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary'; readings weighed: (1) it bars only insufficiency-of-the-verse reasoning, versus (2) it bars any UNDERDETERMINED involving a single pressed verse, including dropped-limb mootness.
why: The judge's stated ground is the defender's dropped limb, not the insufficiency of a single verse to state or contradict a link, so K-S2 is not violated.
